newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London mixed, ADM off, gold quiet.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London mixed, ADM off, gold quiet.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were mixed but slightly pressured on Tuesday after Wall Street registered record highs on Monday only to close lower.
"I think we may see a bit of profit taking after the Dow put on more than 200 points in the last week," one trader said.

The Dow industrials closed 37.32 points or 0.47 percent lower on Monday at 7,858.49, after hitting a lifetime peak at 7,951.45. The yield on the 30-year Treasury bond continued to rise, to yield 6.58 percent.
The September S&P 500 futures contract was trading 0.65 point higher at 919 points at 1054 GMT on Globex.
Archer Daniels Midland Co fell 1/4 to $23 after Standard & Poor's said late Monday it may cut its investment ratings, citing concerns over ADM's ramp-up in investment spending.
Automotive maker Chrysler Corp fell to $33-3/8 from $33-13/16, traders said, after its Japanese unit announced on Tuesday it was recalling 40,754 sport-utility vehicles to repair five faults.
Technology stocks were boosted ahead of results from Motorola Inc, due out later Tuesday, and after gains in U.S. technology shares on Monday, traders said.
Motorola shares gained 7/16 to $81 as analysts expected earnings to grow slightly from the first quarter's $0.53 a share and last year's $0.54 a share.
Telecommunications stocks drew some attention after the Wall Street Journal said the $23 billion merger between Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp was being held up by federal regulators.
The companies are being pressed to take steps in opening their local telephone markets to competition, the newspaper said.
Shares in gold mining companies were quiet, pausing after the steep drop in commodity prices over the last week and a sharp sell-off in gold stocks on Monday.
Mining shares tumbled when gold prices slid to 12-year lows after Australia's central bank disclosed it had sold off about 60 percent of its gold reserves.
Gold prices in London were steady on Tuesday, fixed at $317.60 against $318 on Monday, but analysts forecast prices breaking $300 within three months.
U.S. analysts said they expected government securities, which have helped fuel gains in equities, to push higher in the short term in the face of another round of economic data on Tuesday.

Two weekly reports on U.S. department and chain store sales are out on Tuesday. The Richmond Federal Reserve releases its June index of regional business conditions and the Federal Reserve reports on the level of consumer instalment credit for May.
The next significant piece of economic data is Friday's Producer Price Index for June. Economists predicted the PPI to be unchanged over the month, compared with a 0.3 percent decline in May.
